assertions.evidence: Section 3 defines a full context health metrics table with 7 metrics: context utilization rate (already used tokens / window size), reference freshness (age of cited context in steps), coherence score (cross-turn reply consistency via LLM-as-Judge), token budget, compression event frequency, task drift, and repeated question rate. Each metric has defined normal/warning/danger ranges.

Section 3 includes a complete Python function `detect_context_degradation(session)` that implements 5 detection heuristics: (1) window utilization check with compression trigger, (2) reference freshness check for stale context, (3) decision confidence decline detection via monotonic decrease over 3 steps, (4) repeated question detection via semantic similarity with threshold 0.85, (5) task drift detection via cosine similarity to initial goal embedding. This goes beyond monitoring to active detection with automated responses.

Section 5 defines specific numeric alert thresholds in YAML format: ContextWindowOverflow at utilization > 0.95 for 1m, RepeatedQuestionDetected at rate > 0.15 for 0s, AgentLoopDetected at redundant_rate > 0.5 and call_count > 10 for 1m, ContextUtilizationHigh at > 0.8 for 5m, StaleContextReference at oldest_age > 20 steps for 5m, ConfidenceDecline over 3 consecutive steps, TaskDriftDetected at drift_score > 0.3, and AgentCostSpike at per_session > $1.00.

Section 6 provides a detailed 5-row dashboard layout: Row 1 has 4 overview metric cards (active sessions, task completion rate, avg cost per session, avg response latency with P50/P95/P99). Row 2 has 3 degradation trend charts (context utilization histogram, repeated question rate trend, decision confidence trend). Row 3 has a tool audit table with 6 columns. Row 4 has an anomaly event list with 5 columns. Row 5 has a single-session trace view showing step-by-step decision chain with context and confidence metrics.

Section 10 explicitly defines MTTD targets: repeated question detection < 2 minutes (NLI semantic similarity real-time), context degradation < 5 minutes (utilization trend + reference freshness), loop execution < 1 minute (consecutive call detection + circuit breaker), task drift < 5 minutes, tool call failure < 1 minute, cost spike < 5 minutes. The overall design achieves MTTD < 5 minutes for the primary degradation scenarios.

The solution defines multiple context health metrics across sections 1.1-1.4: context faithfulness score (1 - repetition penalty), information recall rate (successful recalls / expected recalls), conversation coherence score (1 - contradiction penalty - dropped commitment penalty), and conversation efficiency score (based on turns, repeated questions, user frustration). These cover utilization, freshness, and coherence aspects in different but equivalent ways.

The solution includes multiple detection algorithms: (1) `detect_repetition()` in ContextFaithfulnessTracker uses semantic similarity or keyword matching to detect repeated questions, (2) `check_recall()` in InformationRecallMonitor detects when Agent fails to recall previously provided information, (3) `check_contradiction()` in CoherenceMonitor uses LLM to detect logical contradictions, (4) `detect_degradation()` function in section 8.4 checks for decreasing quality scores, sudden changes, and quality drops. These are active detection heuristics, not just monitoring.

Section 9 defines specific numeric thresholds in AlertManager: repeated question count >= 2 triggers high severity, session quality CRITICAL triggers critical severity, session quality DEGRADED triggers medium severity, degraded_session_ratio > 0.3 triggers critical severity. Section 5.2 RealTimeGuard config specifies min_faithfulness_score: 0.7, min_recall_rate: 0.6, min_coherence_score: 0.7. Section 9 metric summary table lists thresholds: faithfulness < 0.5, recall < 0.6, coherence < 0.5, efficiency < 0.5, user frustration >= 2, degraded ratio >= 30%.

Section 5.2 provides an ASCII dashboard layout with 4 panels: (1) Real-time metrics showing active sessions, avg turns, degraded sessions, and health percentage bar, (2) Turn vs Quality trend chart with X-axis as conversation turns and Y-axis as quality score with intervention threshold line, (3) Root cause distribution bar chart showing 5 categories (CONTEXT_OVERFLOW, MEMORY_DECAY, STATE_LOSS, RECALL_FAILURE, UX_DEGRADATION), (4) Alert history timeline with severity levels and timestamps.

The solution defines processing latency requirements per layer (L1: < 200ms, L2: < 30s, L3: hourly) but does NOT explicitly set a Mean Time to Detect target for the degradation scenario. There is no statement like 'degradation should be detected within X minutes.' The layer latencies describe system processing time, not the end-to-end detection time objective for when degradation starts to when it is identified.
